sentence: This project provides equipment and services that help diabetes researchers study islets and other tissues that handle metabolism.
This project tries to detect small gene changes in brain malformations and learn how they affect different cell types in epilepsy.
This project studies whether disrupted body clocks affect how the mammary gland develops, using single cell data to find the key genes.
This project tries to find out why loss of a mitochondrial fission protein harms nerve cell function more than loss of its adapter proteins.
This project tries to build kidney nephrons with blood vessels in culture and in grafted tissues, and a way to test how well they work.
This project studies how ribosomes that collide on messenger RNAs are controlled, and how problems in this control lead to diseases of nerve cells.
This project studies how the Notch pathway and epigenetics drive excess smooth muscle cells in supravalvular aortic stenosis, using mouse models and human cells.
This project provides human genetics and machine learning tools that help researchers study inflammatory bowel disease and other digestive diseases.
This project works to understand and build safe cancer immunotherapies, including cell therapies, by studying how immune cells fight cancer.
This project builds risk models from electronic medical records to find which Veterans are more likely to develop opioid use disorder or overdose.
This project studies how surviving retinal neurons respond to gene replacement therapy and how retinal plasticity affects restored connections in the eye.
This project tries to find the best ways to put cervical cancer prevention into practice for people living with HIV.
This project studies how COVID-19 infection and social factors affecting health relate to brain inflammation linked to depression.
This project tries to find out how a transcription factor in endothelial cells protects blood vessels and the heart from damage caused by cancer drugs.
This project builds patient-specific cardiac organoids, combining computer, chemical and cell models, to test drugs and model heart disease.
This project studies how transcription factors control gene expression, using a small molecule that rapidly breaks down these proteins.
This project studies how the shapes of potassium channel proteins change as they let ions cross the cell membrane.
This project compares the uterotubal junction in women with and without endometriosis and builds a small endoscope to help diagnose endometriosis.
This project uses electronic health records and genetic differences to find which people are at high risk of dying by suicide.
This project builds a blood-brain barrier and glioblastoma chip to test how chemotherapies and immunotherapies reach brain tumors.
